title: Georgia's 14th Congressional District election, 2026
description: This is the regularly scheduled general election for Georgia's 14th Congressional District. The seat became vacant in January 2026 when Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene resigned, and Republican Clay Fuller won the subsequent special election runoff in April 2026 to serve the remainder of the term. Fuller now seeks a full term and won the May 2026 Republican primary, while Democrat Shawn Harris, a retired U.S. Army brigadier general and cattle farmer, won the Democratic primary for a rematch. The district, covering 10 counties in northwestern Georgia from the Atlanta suburbs to the Tennessee border, is considered a safe Republican seat, but Harris has run competitive campaigns focused on kitchen-table issues and bipartisan cooperation.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for the November 2026 general election in Georgia's 14th Congressional District were found as of this writing. Available polling data relates only to the March–April 2026 special election.

candidates.name: Clayton Fuller
candidates.summary: Clayton 'Clay' Fuller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 14th Congressional District, having won the April 2026 special runoff to replace Marjorie Taylor Greene. He previously served as the District Attorney for the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit and is a lieutenant colonel in the Georgia Air National Guard. A former White House Fellow in the first Trump administration, Fuller aligns closely with President Trump and focuses on conservative fiscal policy, border security, and supporting the district's economic interests.

candidates.name: Shawn Harris
candidates.summary: Shawn Harris is a retired U.S. Army brigadier general, cattle farmer, and the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 14th Congressional District. A graduate of Tuskegee University, he served 34 years in the Army and Army National Guard, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. He describes himself as a 'dirt-road Democrat' focused on bipartisan solutions to kitchen-table issues such as rising costs, healthcare, and support for rural communities and veterans.
